_meta.purpose: Step 12, #139 — proves the field_catenation check in src/nl2sql/pipeline/soundness.py. Concatenating two or more distinct fields in the projection fuses values the question almost certainly wants returned separately — a wrong result SHAPE. Flagged as a correction signal.
_meta.format: (candidate SQL, expected verdict) pairs; 'flag' → soundness hit, 'pass' → clean. See null_ordering.json for the catch-rate / false-positive semantics.
_meta.rule: Flag a projection whose || (DPipe) or CONCAT fuses TWO OR MORE distinct columns. Concatenating a single column with string literals (formatting) is not flagged; a bare column is never flagged.

cases.description: first || ' ' || last fuses two name fields — the question likely wants them as separate columns.
CONCAT(fname, lname) is the same field-fusing shape via the function form.
street || ', ' || city || ', ' || zip fuses three address fields into one column.
cases.sql: SELECT street || ', ' || city || ', ' || zip FROM addresses

cases.description: The near-miss negative: one column concatenated with a string literal (formatting) fuses no two fields — must NOT be flagged.
Returning the fields as separate columns is the correct shape — nothing to flag.
A single projected column with no concatenation at all.
